decision: done = a Claim whose player closes the page right after Submit still gets a NIP-03 kind-1040 Bitcoin proof on the leaderboard relays, with no player action
why: owner: players submit and walk away forever; phone-side finalizing was the wrong design

decision: move upgrade + 1040 publishing off the phone into a finalizer that reads the public ots-pending events from relays
why: the pending proof is already public on Nostr, so anyone holding it can finish it; the phone is not needed
evidence: src/ots.js upgradeOts, research doc claim-ordering.md secondary questions

decision: finalizer is a stateless one-shot run every 5 min by a systemd timer on the droplet, relays are the only state
why: idempotent by construction (skip a Claim that already has a 1040), no long-lived socket, tiny memory on a 1 GB box shared with 4 sites; GitHub Actions cron rejected because scheduled workflows get disabled after 60 days of repo inactivity

decision: finalizer also stamps any Claim older than 2 min that has no ots-pending, as a fallback
why: covers a player who closes the page in the second between Claim publish and calendar reply; its calendar time is later, which only costs that player ordering precision

decision: subtract phone-side upgrade, 1040, owed-carrier and k-of-n wait logic; phone keeps stamp-at-Submit and publishes ots-pending signed with the key it already holds
why: two finishers doing the same job is two places for bugs; the phone's stamp gives the earliest calendar time, which is the part only the phone can do

decision: rigor: medium-high. unit + local-relay e2e with a fake calendar for the Bitcoin step, a live upgrade check against real calendars, a dry run against public relays, then deploy
why: deploys a daemon on the shared droplet and writes to public relays; no one-way door (1040 format already fixed), so no arena

decision: finalizer core is pure src/finalize.js (indexEvents, decide, readiness, finalEvent) reusing ots.js/sign.js/verify.js; lives in src/ so the only-sign.js-signs test covers it
why: boundary validation in one place; shell stays thin
result: npm test: 75 pass 0 fail; 5 mutations (digest check, sig check, both time boundaries, at-least-one rule) each fail a test

decision: replace phone's 24 h after first Bitcoin sighting with stateless rule: publish when every calendar in the merged pending attestations is in Bitcoin, or Claim created_at older than 12 h and at least one is
why: finalizer keeps no state between runs; Claim created_at is on the relays, first sighting is not
result: unit test readiness boundary at 12h-1 / 12h passes

decision: an ots-pending with no matching Claim on relays is skipped, never finalized
why: otherwise anyone could make the finalizer sign 1040s for arbitrary digests

decision: finalizer/run.mjs one-shot: 3 relay reads (7d claims, 7d ots-pending, 8d 1040 by #k) plus 1040 by #e for open Claims in chunks of 100; 8 Claims in parallel; dry-run GETs calendars but never POSTs, publishes, or writes the key
why: relays differ on #k indexing; dry-run must be safe to point at public relays
result: test/finalizer.test.mjs 2 pass: 3 runs to one 1040 then a 4th publishes nothing; #k-blind relay sees the 1040 via #e (fails with the #e query removed); fallback stamp publishes 1 ots-pending, dead relay -> exit 0

decision: relay reads time out at 15 s, not fetchEvents' 5 s default
why: first public probe got 0 events from relay.damus.io that answered fine seconds later; a background job can wait
result: dry-run against public relays: claims=0 (relays hold no kind 8064 at all yet)

decision: known gap: if every relay holding the 1040 fails to answer a read, the next run publishes a second 1040 (new created_at, new id)
why: no local state by design; duplicate 1040s for one Claim are harmless to a reader that takes any Bitcoin-attested one

decision: phone stamps only for a newly signed Claim at first Submit; Retry never restamps; record.ots shrinks to {calendars, errors}; old records' ots.file/final/bitcoinSeenAt fields are ignored, not migrated
why: a failed or interrupted stamp is the finalizer's job (fallback stamp after 120 s); live phones keep working with old records
result: npm test 72 pass 0 fail; npm run e2e all checks passed (steps 3 download and 6 owed-carrier removed)

decision: deleted otsStatus and encodeFile from ots.js; kept stampDigest, upgradeOts, merge, pruneToBitcoin, bitcoinCalendars, finalTemplate (finalizer uses them)
why: dead after the phone stopped upgrading
